lessons.title: Amoxicillin — pediatric AOM
facts: Observation 48-72 h is possible at 6-23 months with unilateral nonsevere AOM without otorrhea, or age >=2 with nonsevere AOM without otorrhea, only when reassessment is assured.
gaps: No infant <6 months or pediatric renal table.
Independent clinical/pharmacist review pending; this scoped lesson does not establish all-condition coverage.
lessons.opening: For immunocompetent children >=6 months with confirmed aom requiring antibiotics, when is Amoxicillin — pediatric AOM appropriate, and what complete regimen would you choose?
stages: Confirm syndrome, severity, eligibility and whether antibiotics are indicated
Choose sourced first-line or conditional alternative
Give dose, formulation, route, interval and duration
Check allergy, contraindications, kidney and liver guidance for each component
Review interactions, monitoring, source control and follow-up
Changed patient factors: reassess choice and summarize

regimen.population: Immunocompetent children >=6 months with confirmed AOM requiring antibiotics
regimen.duration: 10 days if <2 years or severe at any age; otherwise 7 days at age 2-5, 5 days above age 5 (UCSF snapshot)
regimen.adjustment: Apply each loaded component safety profile; do not extrapolate to excluded populations.
